result.topic_en: Gauss conjectures that products of expressions $a+b\rho+c\rho^2+\dots$ over the primitive roots $\rho$ of $x^n=1$ can be reduced to the form $(x-\rho y)(x-\rho^2 y)\dots$, works out small cases, then rejects the conjecture as false; he also records that periods of roots of $x^n=1$ cannot share the same form.

items.quote:
Forsan omnia producta
ex $(a+b\rho+c\rho^2+d\rho^3\ldots)$
designante $\rho$ omnes radices prim. [-aequ.-] {+aeqn.+} $x^n=1$
ad formam $(x-\rho y)(x-\rho^2 y)\ldots$
reduci potest.
items.english: Perhaps all products of $(a+b\rho+c\rho^2+d\rho^3\ldots)$, where $\rho$ denotes all primitive roots of the equation $x^n=1$, can be reduced to the form $(x-\rho y)(x-\rho^2 y)\ldots$.

items.quote:
Falsum est
Hinc enim sequeretur e binis numeris e forma
Pr. e $(x-\rho y)$ contentis productum in eadem forma esse
quod facile refutatur
items.english: It is false. For it would follow from this that the product of two numbers contained in the form Pr.(x - rho y) is in the same form, which is easily refuted.

items.quote:
Radicum aeq. $x^n=1$ periodi plures eandem formam habere
non posse demonstratum
items.english: It has been proved that several periods of the roots of the equation $x^n=1$ cannot have the same form.
